_what: Provider-price provenance for the media estimator. Values were read from the official OpenAI documentation.
_how_to_refresh: Re-read the OpenAI model and pricing pages, then run packages/cost/src/media.test.ts. THE IMAGE ROW IS NOT REFRESHED THAT WAY: since 33.1-03 it is MEASURED, not read — re-run the one-call probe recorded in .planning/phases/33.1-*/33.1-PRICE-EVIDENCE.md and take usage.cost from the response.

entries.unit: USD per output video-second, per resolution

vendor.pricingInfoOverride: Sora 2 costs $0.10 per second at 720p. VERIFIED 2026-08-26 against developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing.

entries.notes: OpenAI Videos API. The adapter pins model, prompt, 720x1280 portrait size and an officially supported duration.

succession.whatRemains: 33.1-04 landed the PRICE ROW, the 1-15 duration grid and the repin of MEDIA_DEFAULT_VIDEO. Still to do (plan 33.1-05): the submit path itself - a JSON POST to openrouter.ai/api/v1/videos replacing the multipart api.openai.com/v1/videos call, its 202 -> polling_url -> unsigned_urls[0] poller beside pollOpenAiVideoTask, and the OPENROUTER_API_KEY on the video leg. A repin is NOT a migration: until replacementWiredUp is true a reel still submits to the endpoint being withdrawn, whatever MEDIA_DEFAULT_VIDEO now says.
succession.why: OpenAI is retiring the VIDEOS API ITSELF on 2026-09-24, not merely this model, and names NO replacement. sora-2-pro carries the SAME shutdown date, so the successor cannot be an OpenAI model - which means it amends ADR-024 ('OpenAI is the provider for every media kind') and is an owner decision about where customer prompts are sent. Corroborated 2026-08-26 across developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations and independent trade coverage; announced 2026-03-24. ADR-027 (2026-08-30) supersedes ADR-026's veo-3.1-lite choice: the owner took grok-imagine-video for its 1-15 any-integer duration grid, knowingly accepting xAI as a new recipient of customer scene prompts.

shortlistPricedPerOutputSecond.note: Cheapest, and HALF the sora-2 rate. Owner already holds a GCP credential (ADR-016). ADR-016 currently forbids Veo as a fallback target on ECONOMICS that do not hold for this variant, so it needs a superseding ADR rather than a quiet override.
Per-second on the API side, but yuan-denominated - FX drift inside a USD price table.
2K output at roughly a third of Veo 3.1's full 1080p rate.

rejectedByRule3.why: Bills per MILLION TOKENS, configuration-dependent. Not pre-computable per output second before the request exists, which is exactly what rule 3 refuses.
Shares the 2026-09-24 shutdown. A fallback that dies on the same day as the primary is not a fallback.

entries.unit: USD per output video-second, per resolution

vendor.pricingInfoOverride: xAI's Grok Imagine video on OpenRouter costs $0.05 per second at 480p and $0.07 per second at 720p, for durations of 1 to 15 seconds (any integer). READ 2026-08-30 from openrouter.ai/x-ai/grok-imagine-video, and corroborated the same day by a live paid call: duration 5 at 480p returned usage.cost 0.25, exactly 5 x $0.05.

entries.notes: Route-qualified id: the video plane posts to openrouter.ai/api/v1/videos and the id travels unstripped. No 1080p rate is published, so a 1080p request is unknown_model rather than a silent downgrade. The 1-15 grid is the reason this counterparty was accepted - see ADR-027.

entries.notes: The adapter pins WAV output, voice, and speed 1.
Verbose JSON with word timestamps is requested for caption timing.

vendor.pricingInfoOverride: MEASURED, not quoted: one live OpenRouter call on 2026-08-30 for a 1024x1536 quality:low image returned usage.cost $0.004875 (image_tokens 158 = $0.004740 fixed, plus $0.000135 for a 27-token prompt). Reserved at $0.006 - the extra $0.001125 is prompt-token headroom for ~225 further tokens.

entries.notes: Route-qualified id: the still plane posts to openrouter.ai/api/v1/images and the id travels unstripped. The adapter pins size 1024x1536, quality low, n 1, output_format png. size and NOT aspect_ratio - the same probe showed they are not interchangeable (aspect_ratio 9:16 returns 864x1536 at $0.003735), and the cheaper, better-composed 9:16 option is deferred to its own phase because it changes what every still looks like.

sceneKinds._what: 20.2 §2.3 / ADR-019 — the per-scene-kind economics the scene contract is justified by.
sceneKinds._derived: DERIVED from the provider entries above, not separately sourced. media.test.ts recomputes every number here from the live tables, so the ADR's arithmetic cannot rot silently while a price row moves.

perScene.note: A free-library clip. It BUYS a line (a mediaJobs row and landed bytes) at a price of zero — unlike uploaded_video/text_card, whose `buys` is null because nothing is fetched at all.
A free-library photograph, panned like an animated_image but at zero.

reel30s._what: The §2.3 worked example, REPRICED against the shipped tables. The plan's $1.36-vs-$3.00 predated the gpt-image-2 cutover, and the all-generated column turned out not to exist at all. Repriced on 2026-08-30 (33.1-03) when the still row moved from a guessed $0.01 to a measured $0.006: mixed went $1.24 -> $1.224. Repriced AGAIN the same day (33.1-04) when the clip rate moved from sora-2's $0.10/s to grok's $0.07/s: mixed $1.224 -> $0.864, stockLeaning $0.40 -> $0.28.

mixed.scenes: 3 generated x 4s + 4 stills x 4s + 1 card x 2s
mixed._generatedSeconds: 3 x 4 s = 12, which is EXACTLY MEDIA_GENERATED_SECONDS_CAP. This deck sits ON the boundary with zero slack - a one-second nudge to any generated scene makes it illegal - and media.test.ts asserts that deliberately, because the cap was chosen to keep this deck and media-director.md's worked answer legal as written.

generatedOnly.why: NOT ARITHMETIC ANY MORE. On grok's 1..15 grid a 30 s all-generated deck IS composable (2 x 15 s) and prices at $2.10, which is under the $3.50 job cap - so nothing in the pricing refuses it. What refuses it is MEDIA_GENERATED_SECONDS_CAP (12 s of generated video per reservation, $0.84 at $0.07/s), added by 33.1-04 to restore in code the guarantee the wider grid destroyed. Both numbers are recorded because the mechanism moved: $2.10 is what it would cost, 12 s is what stops it.

stockLeaning.scenes: 1 generated x 4s + 3 stock_video x 6s + 1 stock_image x 8s
stockLeaning._what: The lever the skill body teaches, priced: the same 30 seconds as `mixed` at a third of its picture cost, because four of its five scenes come from a free library instead of a generator.

sceneKinds._targetsUnreachableByGeneratedVideoAlone: UNCHANGED at [15, 30, 60], but for ONE reason now instead of two. Until 33.1-04: 15 and 30 failed the ARITHMETIC (every sora-2 length was a multiple of 4) while 60 failed the JOB CAP ($6.00 > $3.50) - one property asserted through two mechanisms without saying so. Since 33.1-04 all three are refused by MEDIA_GENERATED_SECONDS_CAP = 12, which is below min(TARGET_DURATIONS) = 15, so the property holds for any future target duration rather than only for these three. If this array ever reads [60], the cap did not land.
